analysis:
Siddaramaiah's June 2013 statement described the Naxal problem as 'not very serious' in Karnataka and said only three or four districts were affected. His government simultaneously asked the Centre to declare those districts Naxal-hit so that they could receive central assistance.

SATP's 2013 Karnataka timeline records low-level incidents: an Anti-Naxal Force trooper injured in Chikmagalur in May, a motorbike burnt in Sringeri in June, a van and shed burnt in Kuthlur in November, and an attack on a forest check-post near Sringeri in November. No LWE fatalities are listed for the year.

The comparative judgement is supported by the low intensity of violence relative to states such as Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. The same timeline records a November spurt and an MHA internal note warning that the Maoists were trying to open a new theatre in the Western Ghats, so the statement described the situation at mid-2013 rather than the whole year.
notes: Firstpost was accessible through a reader proxy during research; the direct page returned HTTP 403. 'Not very serious' is a judgement, and SATP records a later 2013 spurt in Maoist activity in coastal and Malnad districts. The claim is rated true only as a comparative description of the low intensity at the time.
